summary: btc-wallet-tools 1.0.3 opens install-time reverse shell to 45.138.12.177:8090
details: The gem declares a native extension at ext/req_throttle_mini/extconf.rb but ships no C/C++ source — the extension exists solely to obtain install-time code execution via `gem install`. extconf.rb Base64-decodes an embedded Ruby payload and evaluates it inside a forked detached process; the decoded payload opens a TCP connection to the hardcoded host 45.138.12.177:8090 and pipes it bidirectionally to /bin/sh via IO.popen, yielding a reverse shell on the installer's machine. Execution is gated by anti-analysis checks that skip CI environment variables, hostnames matching sandbox/firecracker/vagrant patterns, generated-looking usernames, analysis path prefixes (/tmp, /opt/rubygems, /workspace), and systems with /proc/uptime below ~30 minutes, and additionally requires developer-artifact signals (~/.ssh, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.gem/credentials, ~/.bundle) to be present before firing. The extension file terminates with a trivial `create_makefile('btc_wallet_tools_native')` and no sources to build, confirming the extension declaration is purely an install-lifecycle code-execution hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
